description: We are building a row of three two-storey townhouses in Edmonton. Each townhouse has a legal basement secondary suite. The building area is 270 m2. Stick-framed lumber rafters and ceiling joists from the Part 9 span tables (no roof trusses); floor joists span 4.3 m; plain concrete footings and foundation walls from the Section 9.15 tables; no sprinkler or fire alarm system; not on permafrost; the building official has not asked for professional drawings. The longest rafter is a 4.0 m clear span.
known_facts: each townhouse has a basement secondary suite

gold.engineering_reason: Code exception passes: 3 principal units, suites need not count (Div C 2.4.1.1.(1)(b)(ii) and (2)). Acts do not carve out suites, and the code defines a secondary suite as a dwelling unit, so the building has 6 dwelling units, above "4 dwelling units or less" (Architects Act s.2(6)(b)(ii); EGPA s.2(7)(b)(ii)). Design is the practice of architecture reserved by Architects Act s.2(1): a registered architect (or other authorized entity) is required.
gold.limit_source: Architects Act s.2(1), s.2(6)(b)(ii); EGPA s.2(7)(b)(ii); Div C 2.4.1.1.(2) (code-only suite carve-out); Div A 1.4.1.2.(1) Secondary suite definition.

authoring.label: model-constructed, model-checked, not human-verified
authoring.notes: Constructed scenario, not a real case. Gold written from the quoted sources before any system run. Not human-reviewed. Code-vs-Act suite counting divergence.

assumptions: The Acts do not define "dwelling unit"; reading it to include a secondary suite follows the NBC(AE) definition (a suite is "a self-contained dwelling unit") and the fact that the code needed an express carve-out. Professional regulations not read (UNSOURCED whether they carve out suites).
